submitted.rationale: Index 20 (Co0.33Sb0.67, stoichiometric trirutile CoSb2O6) had the highest EQE of the three measured points at 0.055%. MACE puts CoSb2O6 on the hull, so a single-phase trirutile film is expected here. The Co-rich and Sb-rich points both measured about 20x lower, which suggests merit peaks sharply at the trirutile stoichiometry.

rejected.reason: Measured EQE of 0.0035%. This is the Co-rich spinel/Co3O4 region.
Measured EQE of 0.0027%. This is trirutile with excess Sb oxide, and the extra Sb appears to hurt performance.

consultations.verdict: Support: MACE puts trirutile CoSb2O6 on the hull (0 eV/atom), so a single phase should form at Sb=0.667 (index 20). The MEGNet HSE gap of 0.37 eV is probably too low for a Co2+ d7 oxide. Trirutile antimonates are known photoanodes that absorb in the visible range, so I'm measuring the stoichiometric point first.

Moderate support: MACE puts spinel Co7Sb2O12 near the hull (0.03 eV/atom), and its MEGNet gap (1.44 eV) was larger than CoSb2O6's. The trirutile point measured low, so testing the Co-rich spinel composition at index 5 (Sb=0.208) covers a different phase field.

Weak support: MEGNet gives CoSb2O4 (Sb-rich, Sb=0.667) a 1.93 eV gap, which is below the 2.4 eV photon energy and so allows absorption. Measurements show the Sb-rich side beats the Co-rich spinel by about 15x. Index 24 is the trirutile plus excess-Sb region, and it is also the GP-UCB top pick.
